clue.text: Terribly masculine sporting lad's big-chested

indicators.note: to sport something is to wear it, so the lad has the other letters on him, inside his name

parts.note: a lad is a boy
terribly means very, which is so

explanation.surface: A dreadfully macho young athlete shows off his broad chest.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: having a large bust, said loosely of anyone with a big, full chest.

clue.text: Checked and exposed trapping Queen

indicators.note: trapping means catching something within, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: bared means laid bare, exposed
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: The Queen was checked and stripped bare, perhaps on a chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To be checked is to be stopped or blocked, as a way is when barriers are put across it.

clue.text: Tool that's fancy eases cut trimming rose's top

indicators.note: fancy means elaborate, signalling the letters are worked into a new shape
the top of the word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A garden tool smoothly cuts back the top of a rose bush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fancy' rearranges EASESCUT plus R, the first letter of 'rose's'.
explanation.definitionFit: Secateurs are small pruning shears, a hand tool used by gardeners.

clue.text: Guard dog is old lady's pet

parts.note: ma is an informal word for mother, an old lady
a pet is a fit of sulking, a tiff

explanation.surface: The fierce guard dog is just an old woman's beloved pet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pet' looks like an animal, but it is an old word for a sulk or petty quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mastiff is a large, powerful dog breed traditionally kept as a guard dog.

clue.text: Trigger's first with rogues Del and Rodney?

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the name Trigger's

parts.note: rotters are rogues, scoundrels

explanation.surface: A sitcom joke: the dim road-sweeper Trigger is lumped in with the scheming brothers from the same show.
explanation.walkthrough: Del Boy and Rodney Trotter, with their friend Trigger, are characters in the British sitcom Only Fools and Horses; the question mark flags definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Del and Rodney share the surname in the sitcom, so together they are the brothers of that family.

clue.text: Chess piece one jumps over King

indicators.note: in a down clue over means sitting above, so the first piece comes first

parts.note: a roo, a kangaroo, is one that jumps
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: In chess, a knight is the piece that jumps over the king.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the knight, which jumps; the jumper is in fact a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: The rook, or castle, is one of the pieces used in chess.

clue.text: Most cutting exam after tell-tale turned up

indicators.note: after means this piece follows the other
in a down clue turned up means read from bottom to top, reversing the word

parts.note: a rat is an informer, a tell-tale
a test is an exam

explanation.surface: The most hurtful exam comes after a sneak has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses RAT to TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Tart means sharp or biting in remarks, so the superlative is the most cutting.

clue.text: Exclusive lot is terribly exclusive initially

definitions.text: Exclusive lot is terribly exclusive initially

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of each word is taken

explanation.surface: A select group really is very select.
explanation.walkthrough: The first letters of all five words spell the answer, and the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: An elite is a select, privileged group, a lot that keeps others out.

clue.text: More offbeat satire oddly covers outrage

indicators.note: in a down clue covers means sitting on top, so this piece comes first
oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

parts.note: anger is outrage

explanation.surface: Quirky satire raises a public outcry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stranger is the comparative of strange, meaning odder or more unconventional.

clue.text: Rubbish actress almost given new role

indicators.note: rubbish as a verb-like adjective here means badly done, signalling the letters are mangled
almost means the word is not quite complete, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A hopeless actress is dropped and someone else is given her part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' cuts the last S from ACTRESS, and 'Rubbish' rearranges the remaining ACTRES.
explanation.definitionFit: A play is recast when a performer is put into a different part, or a part is assigned to a different performer.

clue.text: Page messenger taking time

indicators.note: taking means the messenger holds the other letter within it

parts.note: a courier is a messenger delivering packages

explanation.surface: A page boy carrying messages takes his time about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Page' looks like a page of a book or a messenger boy, but it is the definition: a page attends a royal court.
explanation.definitionFit: A page is a young attendant at court, one kind of royal attendant or member of a monarch's retinue.

clue.text: Cool match official occasionally cried quietly

parts.note: ref is short for referee, a match official

indicators.note: occasionally means only some of the letters are taken, every other one

parts.note: sh is a call for quiet

explanation.surface: A calm referee now and then wept softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'cried', R and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To cool something, such as a drink or a person, is to revive it with something chilling.

clue.text: Caused upset on hospital department

indicators.note: on means placed after, the second piece following the first

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
ailed means troubled or upset, as in 'what ailed him'

explanation.surface: Something caused distress on a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Caused upset' reads as one phrase, but the definition is 'Caused' alone.
explanation.definitionFit: To entail something is to bring it about as a necessary consequence, so caused is a synonym.

clue.text: Dock facing North River

indicators.note: facing means the first piece sits up against, and before, the second

parts.note: to dock a tail is to cut it off, to sever it

explanation.surface: A dock looks out to the north across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dock' suggests a quay, but here it is the verb to cut off.
explanation.definitionFit: The Severn is Britain's longest river, flowing through Wales and western England to the Bristol Channel.

clue.text: Demure in action getting seduced

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shy word sits within the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
coy means demure, bashful

explanation.surface: A modest person, once roused, ends up seduced.
explanation.definitionFit: Decoyed means lured or enticed into a trap, close in sense to seduced, led astray.

clue.text: Striking and elegant, but for pants …

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, poor, signalling the words are arranged badly

explanation.surface: Linked to the next clue: someone is striking and smart, apart from their underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is British slang meaning rubbish, used here as the anagram signal; the ellipsis joins this clue to 18 across, which also uses pants.
explanation.definitionFit: Something striking makes an impression so strong it is impossible to put out of mind.

clue.text: Beer ends namely in containers here?

definitions.text: Beer ends namely in containers here?

indicators.note: ends means the first and last letters of the word
in means the abbreviation goes inside the containers

parts.note: ewers are jugs, containers for liquid
ie, from Latin id est, means namely

explanation.surface: Where does beer end up in barrels? Here, of course.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer: beer is finished, put in its casks, at these places.
explanation.definitionFit: Breweries are the works where beer is made and then put into casks and bottles.

clue.text: Correct my French taken by a beauty

indicators.note: taken by means held inside the other pieces

parts.note: a dish is an attractive person, a beauty
mon is French for my

explanation.surface: A Frenchman's 'my!' is taken up by a beautiful woman correcting him.
explanation.definitionFit: To correct someone can mean to reprove or rebuke them, which is to scold or reprimand.

clue.text: … changing pants, idea is so cool

indicators.note: changing means the letters of these words are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Following on from the previous clue: changing one's pants is thought to be a good, cool move.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis continues 15 across's underwear story; here 'pants' is part of the fodder rather than the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cool person is calm and unemotional, not swayed by feeling, which is the sense of the answer.

clue.text: Inspires American with, like, acquiring knowledge

indicators.note: acquiring means taking in, so the first piece holds the second

parts.note: as means like
ken means knowledge, range of understanding

explanation.surface: An American stirs others by, like, gaining learning.
explanation.definitionFit: To awaken feelings or interest is to rouse or stir them, so it means inspires.

clue.text: Adult, small below, in pieces

parts.note: A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult
under means below

explanation.surface: A grown-up, with a little one beneath, is torn apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Asunder is an old word for apart, into separate parts, as in 'torn asunder'.

clue.text: Consume, consumed by binges, tippling

indicators.note: consumed by means swallowed up within the following words, which hold the answer

explanation.surface: Drink up, swallowed in bouts of heavy drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To ingest is to take food or drink into the body, so it means to consume.

clue.text: Old Nick relating to skeleton

parts.note: to nick is British slang for to steal

explanation.surface: Old Nick, the Devil, is somehow tied to a skeleton, as in a horror story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' reads as a name for the Devil; split, it gives O and the verb nick, to steal.
explanation.definitionFit: Osteal is an anatomical adjective meaning of or like bone, so concerning the skeleton.

clue.text: God of sex with bronze exterior

indicators.note: exterior means the bronze word forms the outside, round the other

parts.note: tan is a bronze colour, a suntan
it is a coy word for sex or sex appeal

explanation.surface: A sex god with a bronzed skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titans were the older generation of Greek deities, overthrown by the Olympians.

clue.text: Laurence looking terrible in blue?

indicators.note: looking terrible means the name is in poor shape, its letters jumbled

explanation.surface: Laurence looks awful; is he feeling down?
explanation.walkthrough: 'blue' suggests sad, but it is the colour; the question mark admits the play.
explanation.definitionFit: Cerulean is a deep sky-blue shade, so it is an example of blue.

clue.text: Put pressure on sick to get medicine

indicators.note: on means the first piece sits on top of the other in this down clue

parts.note: ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone presses the sick to take their tablets.
explanation.definitionFit: A pill is a tablet of medicine to be swallowed.

clue.text: Popular detective, cocky, coming over brave

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: coming over means turning over, so these pieces are read back to front

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
pert means cheeky or cocky

explanation.surface: A well-liked, swaggering detective arrives and comes across as fearless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming over' reverses DIPERT into TREPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid is a synonym of fearless, describing someone bold in the face of danger.

clue.text: Attach 'cut down bad habit' warning

indicators.note: cut down means shortened, losing a letter from its end

parts.note: to add is to attach or join on
a vice is a bad habit

explanation.surface: A notice is fixed up urging people to give up a harmful habit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut down' trims ADD to AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Advice can be a caution or recommendation about what to do, so a warning counts as one form.

clue.text: Legally giving sanctuary in sacred surroundings

indicators.note: surroundings means the sacred word forms a ring round the other piece

parts.note: holy means sacred
a nest is a snug refuge or sanctuary

explanation.surface: Someone lawfully offers refuge within a holy place, as churches once did.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something legally is doing it lawfully and above board, in a fair and upright way.

clue.text: Bad sport inhibiting one's cheers

indicators.note: inhibiting means holding in, so one piece is kept inside the other
bad means the letters of the word are spoiled into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sore loser stifles their friend's celebrations.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bad' rearranges SPORT into PROST, which holds I; the 's is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German drinking toast, used like the toast you say on raising a glass.
